summary: Lithuania is an EU and Schengen member: EU/EFTA citizens enter freely, more than 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period, and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen visa. The UK government says only one border crossing with Belarus remains open.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area (Regulation (EU) 2018/1806). Canada's travel advice says stays are cumulative and include visits to any Schengen area country within any 180-day period.

source.name: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 listing the third countries whose nationals must hold a visa — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, Article 4(1) — stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period

fee.notes: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. Fee set EU-wide since June 11, 2024.

source.name: Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 establishing a Community Code on Visas, Article 16(1) (visa fee) and Article 1(1) (stays not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period), consolidated to 11 June 2024

fee.notes: For stays over 90 days: work, study and other long-stay purposes. The Migration Department lists the EUR 140 examination fee (EUR 60 for some Ukrainian citizens; several categories, including under-16s, are exempt). It does not state a processing time or how long the visa is valid.

source.name: Migration Department of Lithuania — State fees for services: visas

passportValidity.text: Lithuania follows Schengen rules: the UK government says your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before you arrive and must expire at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area.

source.name: UK FCDO — Lithuania travel advice, entry requirements
Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 (Visa Code), Article 12(b): the travel document of a visa applicant must contain at least two blank pages

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Canada's travel advice says you may be asked to show proof of medical insurance on entry to Lithuania, and may otherwise have to buy health insurance.

source.name: Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 establishing a Community Code on Visas, Article 15(3) — travel medical insurance with minimum coverage of EUR 30 000

onwardTicket.text: The UK government says that at Lithuanian border control British travellers may need to show a return or onward ticket and proof of accommodation.

source.name: UK FCDO — Lithuania travel advice, entry requirements

proofOfFunds.text: Lithuania's reference amount, as published by the European Commission, is €50 per person per day.

source.name: European Commission — Reference amounts required for the crossing of the external border, fixed by national authorities

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border; there is nothing to submit in advance.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Duty-free from outside the EU: 1 litre of spirits and other goods up to €300 (€430 arriving by air or sea). Lithuania applies the EU's lower tobacco limit to land and sea travellers — 40 cigarettes instead of 200.

Goods for your own use bought in another EU country carry no further duty. Above the EU guide levels (for example 800 cigarettes or 10 litres of spirits), customs may ask you to show they are for personal use.

payments.text: No official source we checked describes card acceptance in Lithuania specifically. The European Central Bank's 2024 payments survey found that across the euro area 89% of in-store transactions were, or could have been, paid without cash, and 95% could be paid in cash.

safety.text: The UK government's travel advice does not advise against travel to any part of Lithuania. It says petty crime is common and to beware of pickpockets in busy locations and on public transport, that there have been instances of drink spiking in Vilnius and at festivals, and that some Ukrainian drones aimed at Russia have crossed into Lithuanian airspace.

tips.text: The UK government says only one crossing point with Belarus remains open, Medininkai–Kamenny Log, and only by private vehicle, and that Russian-plated vehicles may enter only for up to 24 hours in transit to or from Kaliningrad. Canada says Lithuania enforces an EU entry ban on vehicles with Russian or Belarusian plates, with exceptions.

The Curonian Spit is divided between Lithuania and Russia's Kaliningrad region. The UK government warns that walking along the Lithuanian part will eventually reach Russian territory, and Canada says the Nida border-crossing point is closed.
Once ETIAS starts, the EU says applications are made on the official ETIAS website or the official ETIAS mobile app; it is not yet in operation.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lithuania?
faq.answer: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely. US, UK, Canadian, Japanese and around 60 other visa-exempt nationalities can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area (ETIAS is not yet in operation). Everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa from the Lithuanian mission serving their place of residence.

faq.question: Can Russian citizens enter Lithuania?
faq.answer: Russian citizens need a Schengen short-stay visa (Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, Annex I). No official source we could read states Lithuania's current entry restrictions for Russian citizens.

faq.question: How much does a Lithuania Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. The Migration Department lists a €140 fee for examining a national long-stay (Type D) visa application.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Lithuania?
faq.answer: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers across the Schengen Area is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once in operation, the €20 travel authorization will be required for visa-exempt travelers to enter.

faq.question: Can I cross into Lithuania from Belarus?
faq.answer: Only with difficulty. The UK government says only one crossing point remains open, Medininkai–Kamenny Log, and only by private vehicle — scheduled buses are not running — and Lithuania denies entry to Belarus-registered cars, with some exemptions.
